WRITTEN ANSWERS TO STARRED QUESTIONS 
Freight charges for De-oiled Rice Bran 
*81. SHRI K.E. ISMAIL: Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to  
state: 
(a) whether the Minister for Food, C ivil Supplies and Animal 
Husbandry of  
the State Government of Kerala has requested the Minister for the 
classification of De-oiled Rice Bran, an important raw material for 
the production of cattle feed from Class 120 to Class 90, in line with 
classification of fodder or under classification 100 along with other 
De- 
oiled meals, so that Kerala Feeds Limited, a State PSU engaged in 
production of cattle feed, can reduce the freight charges and thereby 
reduce the manufacturing cost of the cattle feed; and 
(b) if so, the details thereof and Government’s decision thereon? 
 THE MINISTER OF RAILWAYS (KUMARI MAMATA BANERJEE): (a) Yes, Sir. 
 (b) The matter has been examined and found that presently, De-
oiled rice  
bran is classified at Class -120 under the Main Commodity Head "Oil 
Cakes and  
Seeds." The freight rate of De -oiled Rice Bran has not been increased 
for the last 4 years despite increase in railways input costs of 
operation. In view of the above, it was not possible to accede to 
reduction of 30% in the classification of De Oiled Rice Bran. 
Production of Milk 
*82. SHRI R.C. SINGH: Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased 
to  
state: 
(a) the details of production of milk in the country, State-wise; 
(b) the details of consumption of milk in the country, State-
wise; 
(c) whether it is a fact that due to shortage of milk in the 
country, its price is going up; 
(d) to what extent the National Project for Cattle and Buffalo 
Breeding (NPCBB) is helping in improving production of milk in the 
country; 

 4 
(e) what efforts the Ministry is making to keep the price of milk 
at an affordable level; and 
(f) whether it is also a fact that in view of just 7 per cent 
increase in the population of cows, there is not much scope for 
increase in production of milk in the country? 
 THE MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI SHARAD PAWAR) : (a) The estimated 
production of milk in the country during 2008 -09 was 108.53 million 
tonnes and anticipated production of milk during 2009- 10 is 112.03 
million tonnes. State-wise production of milk for 2008 -09 and 2009-10 
is given in Statement-I (See below). 

 5 
 (b) Details of monthly per capita consumer expenditure on milk and 
milk products for the year 2007 -08 for rural and urban India in 
respect of 17 major States, as estimated by the National Sample Survey 
Organisation (NSSO) is given in Statement-II (See below). 
 (c) No, Sir. The price of milk has increased mainly due to 
increase in prices of cattle feed and fodder. 
 (d) The implementation of NPCBB has contributed to the increase in 
milk productivity and product ion by way of genetic upgradation of 
bovines. Details of major contributions of NPCBB to the increase in 
milk production is given in Statement-III (See below). 
 (e) The Government has taken following measures to keep the price 
on milk at an affordable level: 
 1. NDDB has been allowed to import 30,000 MT of milk powder and 
15,000 MT of Butter Oil/Anhydrous Milk fat (AMF) at 0% import 
duty for use by milk federations and metro dairies in the lean 
months. 
 2. Export incentives under Vishesh Krishi Gram Udyog Y ojna for 
milk and milk products have been withdrawn and it was reduced 
from 7% to 2% for export of oil cake/meal by Government with 
effect from 27.08.2009. 
 (f) Does not arise in view reply at (a) to (e). Moreover, as per 
Livestock Census number of cows ha s increased by 12.2% in the year 
2007 in comparison to 2003. As per the Integrated Sample Survey, 
during the same period total milk production, including cow milk, has 
increased by 18.9%.

Statement-III 
Major contributions of National project on Cattle and Buffalo Breeding 
(NPCBB) to 
 increase in milk production in the country 
• Semen production in the country has increased from 22 million 
to 46 million straws during the period 2000-01 to 2008-09. The 
number of inseminations has increased from 20 million to 44 
million and as per the impact analysis report submitted by 
NABARD, overall conception rate has increased from 20% to 35% 
over the same period. At present 20 million animals are under 
Artificial Insemination (AI) coverage. 

 9 
• Number of animals in milk has increased from 62 million during 
2000 to 75 million during 2008, i.e. about 13 million improved 
milch animals has been added to milch herd of the country. 
• Crossbred cattle population has increased from 20 million in 
1997 to 27.57 million in 2007. 
Attempts of sabotage in trains 
*83. SHRI K.N. BALAGOPAL: Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased 
to state: 
(a) whether the Ministry has taken note of the incident in which 
brake pipe of Nilambur -Shoranur passenger train was found sawed at 
Nilambur station; 
(b) whether the Ministry has also taken note of the incident in 
which explosives were recovered in Ernakulam- Thiruvananthapuram 
Vanchinad Express; 
(c) if so, what is the progress of the investigation; 
(d) whether there is any confirmation of suspected hand of 
external elements behind the incidents; and 
(e) the steps taken by the Railways to strengthen the security 
systems at railway stations and trains in Kerala in the wake of these 
sabotage attempts? 
 THE MINISTER OF RAILWAYS (KUMARI MAMATA BANERJEE): (a) Yes, Sir. On 
8.7.2010, an incident of tampering of brake system by cutting the 
brake and feed pipe hoses of 654 Passenger train (Ex. Nilambur to 
Shoranur) has been reported at Nilambur Railway station in Palghat 
Division of Southern Railway. 
 (b) Yes, Sir. On 08.07.2010, an incident of recovery of a plastic 
bag containing explosive materials from the general compartment of 
train no. 6303 Ernakulam -  Trivandrum Vanchinad Express has been 
reported at Mavelikara Railway station in Trivandrum division of 
Southern Railway. 
 (c) (i) In the incident of Train No. 654 Nilambur -  Shoranur 
Passenger, Government Railway Police/Shoranur registered a 
case vide crime no. 38/10 under section 151 of the 
Railways Act, which was subsequently transferred to the 
Organised Crime Wing of State C rime Branch / Palghat, 
Kerala where a case has been registered vide crime No. 
OCW/PKD/440/CR/2010 under section 151 of the Railways Act 

 10 
1989 and 3 (2) (e) of Prevention of Damage to Public 
Property Act 1984. The case is under investigation. 
  (ii) In the i ncident of recovery of plastic bag containing 
explosive materials in Train No. 6303 Ernakulam- Trivandrum 
Vanchinad Express, Government Railway Police/Kottayam has 
registered a case vide crime no. 23/10 under section 336 
Indian Penal Code, 5 of Explosives S ubstances Act and 164 
of the Railways Act. The case is under investigation. 

 11 
 (d) The cases are still under investigation by State Police. 
 (e) 'Policing' being a State subject, registration of cases, their 
investigation and maintenance of law and order in Railway premises as 
well as on running trains are the statutory responsibility of the 
State Police. The State Police has a separate wing called the 
Government Railway Police (GRP) for dealing with all matters relating 
to law and order on the Railways. 
 Director General of Police/Kerala had convened a high level meeting 
at Trivandrum, which was attended by Divisional Railway Managers and 
Divisional Security Commissioner/Railway Protection Force of 
Trivandrum and Palghat division. The existing security arrangements in 
Railways over Kerala State were reviewed and necessary measures have 
been taken to enhance passenger security particularly in respect of 
sabotage of trains. 
Scam in Railway recruitment examination 
†*84. SHRI MOTILAL VORA: Will the Minister of RA ILWAYS be pleased 
to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that large-scale malpractices took place 
in the  
examination held on 6 and 13 June, 2010 for the recruitment of 
Assistant Station Masters and Loco Pilots; 
(b) if so, the number of people arrested so far in this case; and 
(c) the steps being taken by Government so as to avert recurrence 
of such incidents in future? 
 THE MINISTER OF RAILWAYS (KUMARI MAMATA BANERJEE): (a) to (c) No, 
Sir. However, Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has registered a 
case re garding leakage of question papers only in respect of one 
Railway Recruitment Board (RRB) i.e.  RRB/Mumbai, out of 18 RRBs where 
examination was held for Assistant Loco Pilots on 6.6.2010 and 12 RRBs 
where examination was held for Assistant Station masters on 13.6.2010. 
As informed by CBI, Hyderabad, total 10 persons have been arrested so 
far in this case. The matter is under investigation of CBI. After 
receipt of reports of leakage of question papers, it has been decided 
to carry out technical audit of the system of examination. 
Construction of office of Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti 
†*85. SHRI AVINASH RAI KHANNA: Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether, according to the Comptroller and Auditor General’s 

 12 
(CAG) report, Government has suffered a loss of Rs. 2.5 crores due to 
non-completion of the office of Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti on time; 
(b) if so, whether Government would punish the officers 
responsible therefor; 
(c) if so, by when and if not, the reasons therefor; and 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 

 13 
(d) the plan of Government to avoid recurrence of such losses in 
future? 
 THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SHRI KAPIL SIBAL) : (a) 
Report No. 23 of 2009- 10 of the Comptroller and Auditor Ge neral (CAG) 
states that Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti (NVS) failed t o construct the 
office building and training institute on land acquired in April 2002 
for the purpose, which resulted in avoidable expenditure of Rs. 2. 53 
crore on rent and extension charges. 
 (b) to (d) During the years 2002 -03, 2003- 04 and 2004- 05, 
sufficient fund were not available with NVS even for construction of 
the school buildings. Hence the work of construction of the office 
building was proposed in 2006. Approval of Government was accorded in 
February 2007. Thereafter, NVS had to approach various local 
authorities for necessary clearance. No Objection Certificate (NOC) 
was received from Fire Department, Meerut in October/November 2007, 
approval of drawing from NOIDA Authority was received in February 
2008, No Objection Certificate (NOC) from Airport Authority was 
received in March 2008 and Mining Department of NOIDA gave permission 
in June 2009. In the meanwhile, tender was invited by Central Public 
Works Department (CPWD) for construct ion of building in May 2008, but 
the same was rejected due to high rates. Tender was again invited and 
the work was awarded in March 2009. Construction work started in July, 
2009 after the approval of Mining Department was received. The 
financial loss as pointed out in the CAG report is notional. While, 
Government is committed to expeditious action in all such cases, it is 
also essential to follow the procedures to obtain statutory clearances 
and approvals from various Central, State and local authorities.

 In view of interruption of rail services due to bandhs/strikes, the 
Railways are suffering revenue loss as delays and cancellation of 
trains impact traffic offerings. Railway finances are also affected as 
there has been an increase in the expenditure on law and order issues. 
However, monetary loss to the Railways is not calculated train wise or 
on the basis of punctuality of trains. 
 'Policing on Railways' is a State subject and the maintenance of 
law and order in  
Railway premises as well as on running trains are, therefore, the 
statutory responsibility  
of the State Police, which they discharge through the Government 
Railway Police (GRP)  
of the State concerned. The Railways bear 50% cost of expend iture on 
the GRP. However, Railway is supplementing the efforts of GRP by 
deploying RPF in assisting to control crime in Railways. 
 In addition, the following measures are taken by the Railways for 
security of passengers and smooth running of trains: 
 1. Nominated trains are escorted by Railway Protection Force 
(RPF) and GRP in the vulnerable sections/areas. 
 2. Close co -ordination is being maintained with State 
administration, Police and intelligence agencies to ensure 
smooth running of trains services. 
 3. An integrated security system has been approved to strengthen 
surveillance mechanism over 202 sensitive and vulnerable 
stations of the Indian Railways. 
Elections of Executive Council of AMU 
*87. SHRI MAHMOOD A. MADANI: Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE  
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) the reasons for the elections of the Executive Council of 
Aligarh Muslim University not being held; 
(b) whether it is a fact that Government has given direction to 
the University not to do so; 

 18 
(c) if so, the reasons therefor; and 
(d) whether Government would ensure holding of the elections 
immediately? 
 THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SHRI KAPIL SIBAL) : (a) 
to (d) According to the information furnished by Aligarh Muslim 
University (AMU), there are 

 19 
eight vacancies, in so far as elected representatives are concerned -  
six to be elected by the Court from amongst its members and two to be 
elected by Lecturers from amongst  
themselves - in the Executive Council. The University has intimated 
that the election of two representatives of the Lecturers to the 
Executive Council is proposed to be held shortly. The election of six 
members of the Court to the Executive Council scheduled for 31st

42 new m embers of the Court as well, to be elected on that date 
itself, to participate in the election to the vacancies in the 
Executive Council. The adjourned meeting of the Court scheduled for 
28th March, 2010 was postponed again. 
 The Government has no role und er the provisions of the Aligarh 
Muslim University Act, 1920, in regard to the process of elections to 
the Executive Council of the University.

*88. SHRI D. RAJA: Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Delhi University has introduced 
Semester System of examination for its various courses; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether it is a fact that Delhi University Teachers’ 
Association (DUTA) has been protesting against introduction of 
Semester System; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof , the reasons therefor and 
Government’s reaction  
thereto? 
 THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SHRI KAPIL SIBAL) : (a) 
to (d) According to the information furnished by University of Delhi, 
Semester System has  
been implemented in post- graduate courses conducted by the University 
with effect  
from the academic session 2009 -10 and in 13 under -graduate science 
courses w.e.f. 2010-11 as per the details given in Statement ( See

Delhi University Teachers' Association has been protesting against 

 20

Development of infrastructure in agriculture sector 
*89. SHRI NATUJI HALAJI THAKOR: Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government is contemplating to initiate any ambitious 
programme to develop infrastructure in agriculture; 
(b) if so, the details thereof, State -wise including Gujarat 
State; 
(c) the details of employment opportunities likely to be 
generated in this sector; 
(d) whether Government is likely to take full care of the 
financial aspects; and 
(e) if so, the foreign exchange likely to be earned? 
 THE MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI SHARAD PAWAR) : (a) to (e) 
Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) has been launched on 16th August, 
2007 with an outlay of Rs. 25,000 crores during the Eleventh Five Year 
plan with the objective of, inter alia , incentivizing States to 
increase investment in agriculture and allied sectors, including, for 
creation of agriculture infrastructure. Details of the State -wise 
release of funds for RKVY during 2009- 10 and 2010 -11 is given in 

 22 
Statement-I (See below). 
 Several other schemes of the Ministry of Agriculture include 
components for the development of infrastructure. These schemes 
provide support for, inter alia, construction  
of rural godowns, micro irrigation, marketing infrastructure, post-
harvest management, 

 23 
mechanization, establishment of seeds/fertilizers/soil/pesticides 
testing laboratories, seed processing etc. Details of the State -wise 
release of funds for such major schemes for 2009 -10 is given in 
Statement-II (See below). Expenditure under these schemes is shared 
between the Government of India, the State Governments and the 
beneficiary farmers in the pattern given in Statement-III (See below). 
 Investments in infrastructure in the agriculture sector positively 
impact employment opportunities and earnings from both domestic sale 
and export. Quantified estimates in this regard are not available.

Steps taken by FCI for proper storage of foodgrains 
 The following steps are being taken for proper storage, movement 
and safe upkeep of foodgrains in FCI. 
 (i) All FCI godowns are to be constructed as per specificati ons 
and foodgrains stored by adopting scientific storage 
practices.

to be provided in all the godowns.

out  regularly and timely for the control of stored grain 
insect pests and rodents.

stored on elevated plinths and wooden crates be used as 
dunnage material. Stacks should be properly covered with 
specifically fabri cated low -density black polythene water

by qualified and trained staff of FCI.

to the extent possible so as to avoid longer storage of 
foodgrains in godowns. 
 (vii) Only covered wagons are to be used for movement of 
foodgrains so as to avoid damages during transit. 
 (viii) Proper weighment and accounting are to be ensured at the 
time of receipt and issue of foodgrains. 
 (ix) Insuring transit losses in rail movement of foodgrains by 
rail. 
 (x) Providing escorts while transporting foodgrains from Depot to 
Rail head and vice-versa.

Chinese model of plantation 
561. SHRI N.K. SINGH: Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased 
to state: 
(a) whether Government has decided to follow the Chinese model of 
plantation of paddy and other high yielding seeds to increase the 
production of foodgrains; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the agricultural yield in the country is very low as 
compared to China and if so, the facts thereof; and 
(d) the concrete steps taken by Government to increase the 
agricultural yield in the country? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE  
(PROF. K.V. THOMAS) : (a) to (d) In the consultative Workshop 
organized at Kolkata on 9- 10th July, 2010 on new initiative "Bringing 
Green Revolution in the Eastern India", promotion of hybrid rice based 
on Chinese model was highlighted as one of the main interventions that 
needs to be promoted to ensure increase in rice productivity. India is 
the second country next to China to have successfully commercialized 
hybrid rice technology. 
 The average rice yield in India in lower (about 3.0 t/ha) than in 
China (6.6t/ha). The yield in China are high due to large scale 
adoption of hybrid rice; complete irrigation; higher organic matter 
due to higher use of nutrients; uniform growing conditions; intensive 
cultivation practices adopted by small farmers. In India, rice is 
grown under diverse conditions of which more than 50 percent of the 
area is under unfavourable environment. The area under hybrid rice in 
India is just 3 percent as against 60 percent in China. 
 Apart from the new in itiative on "Bringing Green Revolution to 
Eastern India," wherein states have planned to give thrust to hybrid 
rice promotion; Govt. of India has  
been promoting hybrid rice on a large scale under National Food 
Security Mission -Rice  
(NFSM-Rice), Integrated Cereals Development Programme in Rice Based 
Cropping Systems Areas under Macro Management of Agriculture (MMA), 
Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) etc. 
 As a follow up of the Kolkata workshop, a Task Force at National 

 67 
level for promotion of Hybrid rice has been constituted to prepare a 
work plan for significantly increasing area under hybrid rice. The 
country has already released 43 Varieties of hybrid rice till date 
including 15 hybrid rice varieties from the private sector. It is 
expected that with the strong policy back -up, intensive research and 
active promotion, hybrid rice will be able to cover a large area 
thereby increasing rice production to a great extent.

Gate’ scheme in the country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof;

identified and started functioning in Chhattisgarh; and 
(d) the extent to which the role of middlemen has been reduced

 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

to Home Gate" initiative under Easy Market Scheme to ensure that

reasonable and affordable rates at 15-30% lower than the retail market

Contract farming 
572. SHRI SHANTARAM LAXMAN NAIK: Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government proposes to institutionalize contract 
farming in the  
country; 
(b) the names of States, if any, whether the practice is 
prevalent; 

 83 
(c) whether the concept of contract farming protects the interest 
of land holder farmer; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE  
(PROF. K.V. THOMAS) : (a) Yes, Sir. The Ministry of Agriculture has 
farmed Model State 

 84 
Agricultural Produce Marketing (Development and Regulation) Act, 2003 
and Model State Agricultureal Produce Marketing (Development and 
Regulation) Rules, 2007 for adoption by States/Union Territories 
including the provisions for institutionalized system of contract 
farming. The State Governments of Andhra Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, 
Assam, Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, 
Jharkhand, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Nagaland, Orissa, 
Punjab, Rajasthan, Sikkim, Mizoram, Tamil Nadu, Tripura, and Union 
Territory of Chandigarh have made legal provisions for practice of 
contract farming under their respective State laws. 
 (c) and (d) Yes, Sir. The Model State Agricultural Produce 
Marketing (Development and Regulation) Act circulated by the Ministry 
of Agriculture to the States/Union Territories  
in 2003 for implementation of market reforms, has provisions for 
registration of contract farming sponsors, recording of contract 
farming agreements with the Agriculture Produce Marketing Committee 
(APMC) or a prescribed authority under the Act as well as dispute 
settlement mechanism. It also provides for protection of title or 
rights of the farmers  
over the land under such contracts. These provisions are intended to 
protect the interest of farmer.

576. SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA: Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether any assessment has been made by Government regarding 
losses incurred due to improper use of pesticides and insecticides; 
(b) if so, the details thereof during each of the last three 
years, State-wise; 
(c) whether Government proposes to formulate any scheme to 
educate farmers about judicious use of pesticides and insecticides; 
and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE  
(PROF. K.V. THOMAS) : (a) and (b) No, Sir. Judicious use of registered 
pesticides as per prescribed practices does not harm agricultural 
production. 
 (c) and (d) The Government is promoting safe and judicious use of 
pesticides by adopting Integrated Pest Management (IPM) through a 
scheme "Strengthening and Modernization of Pest Management Approach in 
India". IPM programme under the scheme is implemented throu gh 31 
Central IPM Centres located in 28 States and one Union Territory. 
Pricing of Bt. Cotton seeds 
577. SHRI D. RAJA: 
 SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA:  
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that some States like Gujarat, 
Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh have put restrictions on the pricing of 
Bt. Cotton seeds while there is no such restriction in Punjab, Haryana 
and Rajasthan; and 
(b) if so, whether Government has any proposal to evolve a 
mechanism common to all States to fix the price of Bt. Cotton seeds? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE  
(PROF. K.V. THOMAS) : (a) Out of the nine major cotton growing states 
only three viz. Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat and Maharashtra have sought to 
regulate Bt. Cotton prices within their states through 
Ordinances/Acts. 
 (b) There is no provisions in the Seeds Act 1966 for price 
regulation. Seed is an essential commodity in terms of Seeds (Control) 
Order, 1983 issued in exercise of powers available under the Essential 
Commodities Act, 1955, but only for purposes of quality control and 
price regulation is not provided for. Further, there is no provision 

 103 
for price control in Seeds Bill, 2004. 
Agriculture in hilly areas 
†578. SHRI KAPTAN SINGH SOLANKI: Will the Minister of AGRICULTUR E 
be pleased to state: 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 

 104 
(a)   whether it is a fact that there is substantial difference 
between the agriculture in the planes and the agriculture in the hilly 
areas; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether Government has decided to formulate a new policy 
keeping in view the difficulties being faced in carrying out 
agricultural work in hilly areas; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE  
(PROF. K.V. THOMAS) : (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. There is difference in 
agriculture between planes and hilly areas. The differences are in 
terms of topography, soil type and climatic conditions. Accordingly, 
requirement of varieties of field crops, horticulture crops, input use 
and other agro-technologies somewhat very from the planes to the hilly 
areas. 
 (c) and (d) Indian Council for Agricultural Research (ICAR) has 
already established research institutions in hilly areas as well as in 
plane areas to cater to the needs of technology requirement of farmers 
of both the planes and the hilly areas. The Central Agriculture  
University located in Imphal (Manipur) and Vivekanand Parvatiya Krishi 
Anushandhan  
Sansthan, Almora (Uttarakhand) have exclusive mandate to develop 
suitab
le technology  
for improving agriculture in hilly areas. Many State Agriculture 
Universities whose jurisdictions  
fall in hilly areas have also developed suitable technologies. 
Separate varieties and  
production technologies have been recommended by Indian  Council for 
Agricultural Research (ICAR). 
 Higher subsidy is given to the hilly areas under various Schemes of 
the Government of India. For instance, under the Macro Management of 
Agriculture (MMA), the central assistance for the North Eastern States 
is 100% whereas for the remaining states, the assistance is in the 
ratio of 90:10 between the Centre and the States. Under Grameen 
Bhandaran Yojana, which is a Capital Investment Subsidy Scheme for 
Construction/Renovation of Rural Godowns, higher subsidy @ 33. 33% is 
given to the North Eastern States/hilly areas. 

 105 
 For North Eastern States and hilly areas, the Government of India 
launched a Centrally Sponsored Scheme on Integrated Development of 
Horticulture in the North Eastern States in 2001-02 which was extended 
to Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand during 2003-04. 
This scheme has been renamed as "Horticulture Mission for North -East 
and Himalayan States" with effect from 2010 -11, which provides higher 
subsidy than what is available under Nation al Horticulture Mission 
(NHM) in plane areas. 
 Under NHM also, enhanced assistance is being provided for taking up 
specific activities in the hilly areas of plane states such as 
creation of water resources, creation of post harvest management 
infrastructure etc. and market infrastructure such as wholesale, rural 
markets and retail markets. 

 106 
 In order to make timely availability of seeds at affordable prices 
to the farmers of hilly/remote areas of North Eastern States including 
Sikkim, Himachal Pradesh, Jamm u and Kashmir, Uttarakhand and hilly 
areas of West Bengal, the Scheme of "Transport Subsidy on Movement of 
Seeds" is in operation. 
Inclusion of sericulture in RKVY 
579. SHRI K.N. BALAGOPAL: Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government has decided to include sericulture and 
allied activities in the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY); and 
(b) if so, the details thereof? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE  
(PROF. K.V. THOMAS) : (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. Keeping in view the fact 
that National Commission for Agriculture and Reserve Bank of India 
have considered sericulture up to the stage of cocoon production as an

decided to include sericulture up  to the stage of cocoon production

production in agri-enterprises up to the stage of yarn production and 
marketing to be eligible for funding under RKVY.

 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND 
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (PROF. K.V. THOMAS) : (a) to (d) Central Vigilance 
Committee (CVC) has referred to certain deficiencies/shortcomings in

as inclusion/exclusion errors, diversion and leakages, etc. The study

 Public Distribution System (Control) Order, 2001 mandates the State 
Governments to carry out all required action to ensure smooth 
functioning of TPDS. It stipulates that representatives of State 
Governments or their nominees and the Food Corporation of India (FCI) 
shall conduct joint inspection of the stocks of foodgrains intended 
for issue to ensure that the stocks conform to the prescribed quality 
specifications. It also provides that FCI shall issue sealed sample of 
foodgrains supplied under the Public Distribution System and that the 
fair price shop owne r will display the samples of foodgrains being 
supplied through the fair price shop. 
 Besides, the Government has issued directions to State/UT 
Governments to streamline the functioning of TPDS by enforcing 
provisions of PDS (Control) Order, 2001 and to implement Nine -Point 
action plan which includes, inter alia, use of information technology, 
display of fair price shop- wise and district wise allocation of PDS 
commodities on web-sites for public scrutiny, creating awareness among 
public about PDS operations and training to Vigilance Committees on 
intricacies of PDS operations.

 162 
poor. Under TPDS, foodgrains @ 35 kg./family/month are allocated to 
States/Union Territories for 6.52 crore BPL/AAY families for 
distribution at subsidized prices through Fair Price Shops. Depending

Steps Taken to augment availability of Sugar and Moderate Sugar Prices 
in

• Allowed duty- free import of raw sugar under Advance 
Authorization Scheme by sugar mills on ton- to-ton basis with 
effect from 02.03.2009 upto 30.09.2009.

raw sugar and white/refined sugar. The white/refined sugar has 
been also allowed to be sold at the discretion of the 
importing organizations, but sugar processed from imported raw 
sugar is subject to accelerated releases.

Statement 
Measures taken by the Government to contain price rise 
 Steps taken by the Government to contain price rise in essential 
Commodities are briefly stated below: 
1. Fiscal Measures 
 (i) Reduced import duties to Zero-for rice, wheat, pulses, edible 
oils (crude); and butter and ghee. 
 (ii) Reduced import  duties on refined and hydrogenated oils and 
vegetable oils to 7.5%;

up to 01.08.2009 by sugar mills (notified on 17.04.2009) 
extended up to 31.12.2010. Furthermore, import of raw sugar 
has been opened to private trade up  to 31.12.2010 for being 
processed by domestic factories on job basis. 
 (iv) Allowed import of white/refined sugar by STC/MMTC/PEC and 
NAFED up to 1 million tons by 01.08.2009 under O.G.L. at zero 
duty (notified on 17.04.2009). Furthermore, the duty free 

 172 
import of white/refined sugar under OGL has been opened to 
other Central/State Government agencies and to private trade 
in addition to existing designated agencies. The cap on the 
quantity to be imported upto 31.03.09 has also since been

white/refined  
sugar.

Deficiency in PDS 
†610. SHRI SHIVANAND TIWARI: 
 SHRI RAVI SHANKAR PRASAD: 
Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that improvements are r equired in the 
Public Distribution  
System, presently being implemented in the country due to large scale 
shortcomings within  
it; 
(b) if so, the reaction of Government thereto; 
(c) whether it is also essential to improve the system before 
implementing the National Food Security Bill; and 
(d) if so, the reaction of Government thereto and the details of 
the suggestions that are under consideration for improving the system? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND 
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (PROF. K.V. THOMAS) : (a) to (d) Targeted Public 
Distribution System (TPDS) is implemented jointly by Government of 
India and State/Union Territory (UT) Governments with sharing of 
responsibilities in this regard. The Central Government has taken the 
responsibility for procurement, storage, transportation and bulk 
allocation of foodgrains to the States and UTs. The responsibilities 
for allocation of foodgrains within State/UT, identification of 
eligible Below Poverty Line (BPL) families based on estimate s of 

 189 
Planning Commission, issuance of ration cards to them and distribution 
of allocated foodgrains to eligible ration card holders through fair 
price shops and supervision of the functioning of Fair Price Shops, 
etc., rest with the State/UT Governments. 
 The Evaluation studies on functioning of TPDS got done by the 
Department, has revealed certain shortcomings in the functioning of 
TPDS. 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 

 190 
 Public Distribution System (Control) Order 2001 mandates the S tate 
and UT Governments to carry out all required action to ensure smooth 
functioning of TPDS. 
 Strengthening and streamlining of TPDS is a continuous process. To 
improve functioning of TPDS, Government has been regularly requesting 
State/UT Governments fo r continuous review of lists of BPL and AAY 
families; ensuring timely availability of foodgrains at fair price 
shops; ensuring greater transparency in functioning of TPDS; improved 
monitoring and vigilance at various levels; and introduction of new 
technologies such as Computerization of TPDS operations at various 
levels. 
 The proposed National Food Security law envisages entitling every 
BPL family to a certain quantity of foodgrains per month at subsidized 
prices. The proposed law will also be used to bring about broader 
systemic reforms in the PDS.

Price rise of essential commodities 
614. SHRI SHANTARAM LAXMAN NAIK: Will the Minister of CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government has analysed recent rise in prices of 
various commodities; 
(b) if so, the conclusion arrived with respect to rise in price 
of each of the commodity; 
(c) whether Government proposes to chalk out a policy to meet 
such situations, on permanent basis; 
(d) whether there were cases of artificial shortage created by 
the hoarders; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND 
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (PROF. K.V. THOMAS) : (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. 
Government has analysed the recent rise in prices of essential 
commodities. The retail prices of some of the essential commodities 
such as atta, pulses such as urad dal, tur dal, edible oil such as 
groundnut oil, vanaspati, potato and onion had increased over the last 
3 months in 4 metros viz. Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai. The 
details of retail prices of essential commodities in 4 Metros viz. 
Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai is given in Statement -I ( See 
below). 
 The increase in prices of wheat can be attributed partly due to the 
increase in MSP. 
 Domestic prices of pulses rose mainly on account of decline in 
production of pulses. In 2008 -09, production of pulses decline to 
14.57 million tonnes as compared to 14.76 million tonnes in the 
previous year. The domestic production of Urad, Tur and Moong had 
declined to 1.17 million tonnes, 2.27 million tonnes, and 1.04 million 
tonnes during 2008-09 as compared to 1.46 million tonnes, 3.08 million 
tonnes and 1.52 million tonnes during 2007-08 (Final Estimates). 
 Increase in prices of edible oil has been due to additional demand 
of edible oils in the domestic market for the upcoming festi val 
season. Production shortage in 2009 -10 has reflected in increase of 
prices of ground nut oil. 
 (c) Government takes several proactive measures as and when the 
situation of price rise arises. Government has already taken several 
short term fiscal and administrative measures to contain the price 

 202 
rise of essential commodities which are given in Statement -II. [Refer 
to the statement appended to answer to unstarred questions No. 596 
Part-(e)]. 
 (d) No specific case relating to artificial shortage created by 
the hoarders has come to the notice of the Government. 
 (e) Does not arise.

Affiliating university system 
627. DR. JANARDHAN WAGHMARE: Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government is aware of the fact that the affiliating 
university system is outdated and does not allow universities to do 
research seriously; 
(b) whether Government is also aware that the National Knowledge 
Commission (NKC) has recommended to establish Central and State Boards 
of Undergraduate Education to replace the affiliating university 
system; and 
(c) if so, the steps being taken to move in this direction? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIMATI D. PURANDESWARI) : (a) Universities are required to perform 
various functions, which include tea ching, research, extension and 
conduct of examination. University Grants Commission (UGC) has 
notified (Affiliation of Colleges by Universities) Regulations, 2009 
in order to regulate and standardize the process of granting 
affiliation to Colleges by the Universities. 
 (b) and (c) Yes, Sir. However, there is no agreement on this aspect 
of the recommendations of National Knowledge Commission. Establishment 
of a Central Board of Undergraduate Education along with State Board 
of Undergraduate Education may als o impose a lower common denominator 
on higher education at the undergraduate level, and would be against 
autonomy of higher educational institutions. In addition, it would not 

 232 
only divorce undergraduate higher education from the postgraduate 
studies and research, but would also lead to over- centralization, 
leading to adverse consequences on the relevance and updating of 
curriculum and, therefore, it is felt that undergraduate education 
must remain as integral part of the University System.

Revamping plan for education 
629. MS. MABEL REBELLO: 
 DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY: 
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether the Ministry has failed to implement his revamping 
plan on education reforms; 
(b) if so, the reasons for not implementing revamping plan for 
education; 
(c) if so, to what extent reforms of education have been 
considered and whether implementation of compulsory education has not 
so far taken a final shape; and 
(d) if so, the reasons and by what time education to all will be 
implemented? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIMATI D. PURANDE SWARI) : (a) to (d) Educational reforms are a 
continuous process and Eleventh Five Year Plan seeks to carry them 
forward through expansion, inclusion and rapid improvement in quality 
through institutional and policy reforms and by enhancing public 

 234 
spending. There will be no Class X Board examination w.e.f.  2011 for 
students studying in CBSE’s Senior Secondary Schools an d who do not 
wish to move out of the CBSE system after Class X. The students 
studying in CBSE’S Secondary Schools will be required to appear in 
Board’s external examination if they intend to leave the Secondary 
School after Class X. The Continuous and Comp rehensive Evaluation has 
been strengthened in all CBSE affiliated schools w.e.f. October, 2009 
in Class IX. The new Grading System has been introduced at Secondary 
School Level (for Class IX and X) effective from 2009 -10 academic 
season. During various mee tings with stakeholders, survey etc. the 
CBSE has received encouraging response. 

 235 
 Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) follows a holistic approach to improve 
the quality of elementary education and subject to certain norms, 
provides for opening of new primary scho ols, upgradation of primary 
schools to upper primary schools, construction of school buildings, 
construction of additional classrooms to improve the students 
classroom ratio, recruitment of additional teachers to improve the 
pupil teacher ratio, in-service training of the teachers and training 
of the teachers and training of untrained teachers, provision of text 
books, learning enhancement programme, remedial teaching, school and 
teacher grant and regular academic support to the school through Block 
Resource Centres and Cluster Resource Centres to improve the quality 
of classroom practices. 
 Model Degree Colleges are being established one each in 374 
educationally backward districts with low GER. These colleges will 
predominantly serve rural areas and distri cts with concentration of 
population of SC/ST/Minorities. 
 UGC has taken a number of steps to bring in academic reforms in the 
Central and State Universities such as examination reforms including 
continuous internal assessment, introduction of credit- based courses, 
semester system, institutional mobility of students, credit 
accumulation and credit transfer, regular updating of curricula etc. 
 The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 
which provides for free and compulsory education to  all children in 
the age group of six to fourteen years and the Constitution Eighty -
sixth Amendment Act have come into force from 1st April, 2010.

Establishment of educational institutions 
631. SHRI BHAGAT SINGH KOSHYARI: Will the Minister of HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 

 244 
(a) what is the policy relating to establishment of an 
educational institution in the country; and 
(b) the status of the institutions that are being announced to be 
opened in the State of Uttarakhand? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIMATI D. PURANDESWARI) : ( a) Education is a subject on the 
Concurrent List of the Constitution, it is the shared responsibility 
of both the Central and the State Governments. Establishment of an 
educational institution in a State/UT is the primary responsibility of 
the State/UT Government. A university is established or incorporated 
by or under a Central Act or a State Act or an institution is declared 
as Deemed to be University by the Central Govt. The technical 
institutions that come under the purview of All India Council for 
Technical Education (AICTE) are established by Public Private Trusts, 
Registered Societies and/or Central/State Governments. However, AICTE, 
grants approval to new technical institutions in terms of provisions 
under Section 10(k) of AICTE Act. The National Policy of Education 
(NPE), 1986  
(as modified in 1992) provides for a National System of Education, 
which implies that up to a given level, all students, irrespective of 
caste, creed, location or sex, have access to education of a 
comparable quality. The NPE envisages education essential for all as a 
fundamental to all round development - material and spiritual. 
 (b) Eleventh Five Year Plan document of Department of Higher 
Education envisages establishment of Indian Institute of Management 
and National Institute of Technology each in the State of Uttarakhand. 
Action has already been initiated in this regard. Under the Sub-
Mission on Polytechnics Scheme, one Polytechnic has bee n approved in 
Pithoragarh district of Uttarakhand for which partial financial 
assistance has been released. In addition, two educationally backward 
districts of Uttarakhand have been identified for establishment of 
Model Degree Colleges. The proposals from  State Govt. have not been 
received so far in this regard. HNB Garhwal University has already 
been converted into a Central University under the Central 
Universities Act, 2009 which came into force on 15.01.2009. AICTE has 
approved 3 institutions in the State of Uttarakhand for the year 2010-
11 viz. Devshali Vidyapeeth College of Management;  
Sela Qui Academy of Higher Education (SelaQui Institute of Engg. and 
Technology and SelaQui Institute of Management); and Maya Institute of 

 245 
Technology and Management.

studies as a percentage of population in the age cohort group of 18-24 
year. The GER for higher education in the country is estimated to be 
12.4%. According to the information available from the website of 
United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation 
(UNESCO), the GER for the world on average is 26%. 

 247 
 (c) to (e) The Eleventh Five Year Plan document targets the 
achievement of GER of 21% by the term inal year of the Twelfth Plan 
with an interim target of 15% by the end of the  
Eleventh Plan. During the Eleventh Five Year Plan, establishment of 
Central Universities in hitherto uncovered States has been envisaged. 
The Strategy for increasing enrolment includes 

 248 
establishment of new institutions of higher learning in the Central 
sector such as Indian Institutes of Technology, Indian Institutes of 
Management, National Institutes of Technology and Schools of Planning 
and Architecture, incentivizing States f or establishment of new 
institutions by establishment of model degree colleges in districts 
where the GER is below the national level and expansion of existing 
institutions by policy interventions and schemes aimed at increasing 
access and opportunities for pursuit of higher education.

years of age has not been admitted in any school or through admitted, 
could not complete his or her elementary education, then, he or she

provides that a child so admitted to elementary education shall be 
entitled to free education till completion of elementary education 
even after fourteen years.

Unhygienic food under Mid-Day-Meal scheme 
650. SHRI TARIQ ANWAR: Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government is aware that unhygienic food is being 
served to school children under Mid-Day-Meal scheme in Bihar; 
(b) if so, the number of complaints received in this regard; and 
(c) the corrective measures taken to provide hygienic food under 
Mid-Day-Meal scheme to school children? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIMATI D. PURANDE SWARI) : (a) and  (b) As per the information 
provided by Govt. of Bihar some complaints had been received in 
districts Sitamarhi, Saran, Patna, Vaishali, Nalanda regarding serving 
of unhygienic food. After enquiry on the complaints, due action has 
been taken. First Information Reports have been lodged and concerned 
Headmasters have been suspended. 
 (c) The overall responsibility to provide wholesome and nutritious 
food to the children in schools under the Mid Day Meal Scheme lies 
with the State Governments/Union Territory A dministrations. The Govt. 
of Bihar has informed that directions have been given to all districts 
to take necessary measures to serve only hygienic meals to the 
children. Cooking cost has been increased to improve the quality of 
food. Schools are being inspected regularly by the state, district and 
block level officers. Headmasters have been instructed to ensure that 
the hot cooked meal is served to the children only after getting it 
tasted by 2-3 adults.

651. SHRI PRAKASH JAVADEKAR: Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that some States have rejected higher 
education bill; 
(b) if so, which are those States and the reasons they have cited 
for this; and 
(c) what is Government doing now in this regard? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIMATI D. PURANDE SWARI) : (a) to (c) No, Sir. The Government has 
constituted a Task Force to aid and assist the Government in drafting 
the Higher Education and R esearch Bill, 2010. The draft Bill as 

 286 
prepared by the Task Force was discussed at the meeting of Central 
Advisory Board of Education (CABE) held on 19th June, 2010. There was 
general consensus with regard to the need to establish an overarching 
body at the Apex level to prevent fragmentation of Higher Education 
and to promote interdisciplinary pursuits for creating new knowledge. 
CABE decided that State Government could send in written comments and 
suggestions within 4 weeks, so that the Task Force could take the same 
into consideration, before the draft Bill is finalized by it and 
submitted to the Central Government.

 The time of four weeks given to the States to respond expired on

rejected the Bill.

Rebate for Khadi products 
659. PROF. P.J. KURIEN: Will the Minister of MICRO, SMALL AND 
MEDIUM ENTERPRISES be pleased to state: 
(a) the percentage of rebate and special rebate, if any, fixed 
for retail of Khadi products and textiles for the Financial Year 2010-

 295 
11; 
(b) whether any decision has been taken to discontinue the rebate 
given by Central Government for the retail of Khadi products; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; 
(d) the total number of workers in the Khadi and Village 
Industries sector; 

 296 
(e) whether discontinuation of rebate by Central Government would 
be advantageous to Khadi workers; 
(f) whether Government proposes to introduce any new scheme for 
the development of Khadi sector, in view of its poor condition; and 
(g) if so, the details thereof? 
 THE MINISTER OF STAT E IN THE MINISTRY OF MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM 
ENTERPRISES (SHRI DINSHA J. PATE L) : (a) to (c) In order to promote 
market for khadi products, the Government had continued through the 
Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) a policy of rebate on 
sale of khadi and khadi products till 2009 -10. Normal rebate @1 0% of 
sales used to be given throughout the year whereas a special rebate of 
additional 10% used to be given for 108 days in a year coinciding with 
Gandhi Jayanti and / or local festivals. However, on the 
recommendations of Expert Committee and after tryin g several pilot 
projects and extensive consultations with stakeholders, the Government 
has introduced a more flexible scheme, namely, Market Development 
Assistance (MDA) Scheme on production of khadi in place of existing 
scheme of Rebate on Sales with effe ct from 01.04.2010 for 
implementation by KVIC during 2010- 11 and 2011- 12. The scheme 
envisages financial assistance @ 20% of production value on khadi and 
polyvastra which will be shared among artisans, producing institutions 
and selling institutions in the ratio 25:30:45. Under the new system 
of MDA; sales are expected to be evenly spread throughout the year, 
the institutions will have the flexibility to use the assistance in 
improving the outlets, products giving incentive to customers, etc. 
 (d) As per data compiled by KVIC, there are about 1.08 crore 
workers engaged in the khadi and village industries sector, including 
an estimated 9.81 lakh artisans alone in the khadi sub-sector. 
 (e) The erstwhile scheme of rebate on sales caused delay in paying 
incentives to the institutions in the sense that they would have to 
wait till sale and wait till next year to get the claims reimbursed. 
Under MDA, incentive would be provided immediately after production of 
the items and this is expected to ease out the working capital 
situation of the institutions by ensuring immediate liquidity which 
would in turn ensure timely payment to the artisans. The newly 
introduced MDA scheme has a provision of sharing 25% of the assistance 
(MDA) with the artisans as incentive or bonus in addition to their 
wages through their bank accounts or post Office accounts. With these 
measures, the sector is expected to grow at a faster pace ultimately 
benefiting the artisans. 

 297 
 (f) and (g) For the development of khadi sector, the Government, 
through KVIC, has introduced several other new schemes, in addition to 
MDA scheme for khadi and polyvastra, namely, ‘Workshed Scheme for 
Khadi Artisans’ for providing assistance for construction of worksheds 
for better work environment and the ‘Scheme for enhancing productivity 
and competitiveness of Khadi Industries and Artisans’ to assist 200 
khadi institutions to make khadi industry competitive with more market 
driven and profitable production by replacement of 

 298 
obsolete and old machinery and equipment and ‘Strengthening of 
Infrastructure of existing Weak Khadi Institutions and Assistance for 
Marketing Infrastructure’ which includes strengthening of 
Infrastructure’ of existing 100 weak selected khadi institutions. 
Besides, the recently introduced Khadi Reforms and Development 
Programme funded by the Asian Development Bank also provides for 
revitalization of khadi sector through measures which, inter alia , 
include enhanced employment and earnings of the artisans through their 
capacity building and empowerment.
